problems.title: A least common multiple plus a greatest common divisor
problems.question: Find lcm(18,15)+gcd(48,45).
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Use the largest prime exponents for the lcm and the common smallest exponents for the gcd.
steps: 18=2×3² and 15=3×5, so their lcm is 90. The gcd of 48 and 45 is 3. Add to obtain 93.

problems.title: A remainder after subtracting products
problems.question: Find the remainder of $11\cdot13\cdot15\cdot17\cdot19-12\cdot14\cdot16$ on division by 13.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Replace each factor by its remainder modulo 13.
steps: The first product contains 13 and has remainder 0. The second has remainder $(-1)\cdot1\cdot3=-3$. Subtracting gives remainder 3.

problems.title: Three rays with an unstated interior condition
problems.question: Rays a,b,c have angle (a,b)=40° and angle (c,b) 24° smaller than angle (a,c). Find angle (a,c).
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: If c is inside the 40° angle, the two smaller angles sum to 40°. Otherwise the three smaller pairwise angles can sum to 360°.
steps: Let x=angle(a,c), so angle(c,b)=x−24°. For the interior position, x+x−24=40, giving x=32°.
Another placement has x+(x−24)+40=360, giving x=172°. For example a at 0°, b at 40°, c at 188° realizes it.
The listed choice is 32°, but the text alone also allows 172°.
problems.answer: $32^\circ$ among the choices; $172^\circ$ is also possible.
problems.note: The source does not say that ray c lies inside the 40° angle. Without that restriction there are two valid angle values.

problems.title: Bisectors beside a right angle
problems.question: O lies on line AB. Rays OC,OD enclose 90° above the line as drawn. Find the angle between the bisectors of AOC and BOD.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Angles above a straight line sum to 180°.
steps: Let AOC=u and DOB=v. Then u+90+v=180, so u+v=90.
The requested angle is u/2+90+v/2=135°.

problems.title: Count divisors of an lcm
problems.question: A=lcm(90,144). How many positive divisors does A have?
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: If $N=p^a q^b r^c$, its divisor count is $(a+1)(b+1)(c+1)$.
steps: The divisor count is 5×3×2=30.

problems.title: Mixed numbers and decimal division
problems.question: Evaluate $(4-3.5(2\tfrac17-1\tfrac15))/0.14$.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions before calculating.
steps: $15/7-6/5=33/35$. Multiplying by 7/2 gives 33/10.
The numerator is 4−3.3=0.7. Divide by 0.14 to get 5.

problems.title: Evaluate a custom operation
problems.question: $a\nabla b=(a/b-b/a)a^2b^2$. Find $2.5\nabla1.5$.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: For nonzero a,b, $(a/b-b/a)a^2b^2=ab(a^2-b^2)$.
steps: ab=15/4 and a²−b²=25/4−9/4=4. Their product is 15.

problems.title: Supplementary angles with a linear relation
problems.question: Four times one supplementary angle is 40° greater than the other. Find the larger.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
steps: Substitute y=180−x: 5x=220, so x=44° and y=136°.

problems.title: Two angle bisectors between parallel lines
problems.question: BE is parallel to AD. AC bisects BAD and CD bisects ACE, as drawn. ADC=74°. Find ABC.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Alternate angles between parallel lines are equal; a bisector halves an angle.
steps: DCE=ADC=74°, hence ACE=148°. Since AD is parallel to CE, CAD=180−148=32°.
AC bisects BAD, so BAD=64°. The adjacent angle ABC is 180−64=116°.

problems.title: Triangles with vertices on two lines
problems.question: Four points lie on one line and three on a parallel line. Count triangles with these vertices.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Choose two points from one line and one from the other.
steps: The count is $\binom42\cdot3+\binom32\cdot4=18+12=30$. No three selected on the same line form a triangle.

problems.title: Inverse-proportional shares
problems.question: Divide 0.6 inversely proportional to 5/2,5/3,5/7. Find the largest part.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Inverse proportionality uses the reciprocals, giving ratio 2:3:7.
steps: The ratio units total 12, and the largest share is $0.6\cdot7/12=7/20$.

problems.title: Minimum overlap of three language groups
problems.question: Of 40 tourists, 65% speak German,85% French,70% English. What is the minimum number speaking all three?
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: If t people belong to all three groups, total memberships are at most $2(40-t)+3t=80+t$.
steps: The memberships total 26+34+28=88, so t≥8.
This bound is attainable: take 8 speaking all three,14 French and English only,6 German and English only,12 German and French only. The group totals are correct.

problems.title: Vertical angles and a one-to-four split
problems.question: In the diagram AOB and COD are vertical angles totaling 110°. OE divides COD in ratio COE:EOD=1:4. Find BOE.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Vertical angles are equal; adjacent angles on a straight line supplement each other.
steps: COD=55°, so COE=11°. OB and OC are opposite rays, hence BOE=180−11=169°.

problems.title: Constant-rate wall work
problems.question: Covering 2/5 of a wall takes 2 h 40 min. What fraction is covered in 3 h 20 min?
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: At constant rate, work is proportional to elapsed time.
steps: The times are 160 and 200 minutes. The fraction is $(2/5)(200/160)=1/2$.

problems.title: Minimum number of bounded summands
problems.question: At least how many summands, each at most 7.6, can total 54.16?
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: n summands can total at most 7.6n.
steps: Seven summands reach at most 53.2, too small. Eight suffice: seven 7.6s and one 0.96 total 54.16.

problems.title: Combine two segment ratios
problems.question: Points are ordered A,B,C,D, with AB:BC=1:2 and BC:CD=3:4. Find AD:BC.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: $AD=AB+BC+CD$.
steps: Divide by BC: $AD/BC=1/2+1+4/3=17/6$.

problems.title: A square between parallel lines
problems.question: Use the source diagram: the top connector makes 16° with the upper parallel and 42° with a square side; the lower connector makes 38° with the lower parallel. Find the marked angle x.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Adjacent square sides are perpendicular; the parallel lines have the same direction.
steps: The top square side points 42−16=26° below the horizontal. The adjacent side, pointing up from the lower right corner, makes 90−26=64° above it.
The lower connector points 38° below the horizontal. The marked angle is 64+38=102°.

problems.title: A product with neither factor ending in zero
problems.question: Two positive integers multiply to 8000 and neither ends in zero. Find their sum.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: $8000=2^6\cdot5^3$; a number ends in zero iff it contains both factors 2 and 5.
steps: All powers of 2 must go to one factor, and all powers of 5 to the other; otherwise a factor would contain 10.
Thus the factors are 64 and 125, with sum 189.

problems.title: A remainder from two congruences
problems.question: m leaves remainder 3 on division by 5; n leaves remainder 2 on division by 3. Find the remainder of 3m+5n on division by 15.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Write m=5u+3 and n=3v+2.
steps: $3m+5n=15(u+v)+9+10=15(u+v+1)+4$. The remainder is 4.

problems.title: Three collinear pieces
problems.question: M,K,P,N are in that order; MP:NK=2:3, KP=PN and MN=28. Find MK.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Let MK=x and KP=PN=t.
steps: $(x+t)/(2t)=2/3$ gives 3x=t. Then MN=x+2t=7x=28, so x=4.

problems.title: Homework after two sets of multiples
problems.question: Among problems 1–50, multiples of 6 are done in class, then remaining multiples of 4 as independent work. How many remain for homework?
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Inclusion-exclusion: count multiples of 6 or 4, subtract multiples of lcm(6,4)=12 once.
steps: The excluded count is 8+12−4=16. Thus 50−16=34 problems remain.

problems.title: Clock hands at twelve twenty-four
problems.question: Find the smaller angle between the clock hands at 12:24.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Minute-hand angle=6m degrees; hour-hand motion=0.5m degrees after 12.
steps: The minute hand is at 144° and hour hand at 12°. Their difference is 132°, already smaller than 180°.

problems.title: Dilute a sugar syrup
problems.question: How much water must be added to 24 litres of 15% syrup to make 9% syrup?
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Sugar amount stays constant: $0.15\cdot24=0.09(24+w)$.
steps: The sugar amount is 3.6 litres in the concentration model. The final volume must be 3.6/0.09=40 litres.
Therefore w=40−24=16 litres.

problems.title: A removed member of ten consecutive integers
problems.question: Ten consecutive positive integers lose one member, leaving sum 2021. Find the removed number.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
formulas: Write the integers n through n+9 and the removed one n+k, where 0≤k≤9.
steps: The remaining sum is 10n+45−n−k=2021, hence 9n−k=1976.
Because 0≤k≤9, we need 1976≤9n≤1985. The only multiple of 9 in this interval is 1980, so n=220,k=4. The erased number is n+k=224.

problems.title: A telescoping fraction sum
problems.question: Evaluate $1/2+1/6+1/12+1/20+1/30+1/42+1/56$.
problems.idea: Translate the data into a simple relation, calculate, and check all permitted cases.
steps: These are the terms k=1 through 7. All intermediate fractions cancel, leaving 1−1/8=7/8.
